The '''Dawn Pyramid of Aargau''' was a large structure on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Aargau/Legends|Aargau]] that was built by a [[Species/Legends|species]] called the [[Sharu/Legends|Sharu]]. Like other constructions of their [[Unidentified Sharu civilization|civilization]], the [[pyramid]] was made of indestructible, iridescent [[Plastic/Legends|plastic]]. When the [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Vicendi]] listed the [[Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy]] in his [[10,000 BBY]] publication, the ''[[Arturum Galactinum]]'', the Dawn Pyramid was included.

==Description==
Built by the [[Sharu/Legends|Sharu]] [[Unidentified Sharu civilization|civilization]],<ref name="Builders" /> the Dawn Pyramid was located on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Aargau/Legends|Aargau]] in the [[Zug system/Legends|Zug system]], located at coordinates L-10 in the [[Arrowhead]] region of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="Atlas" /> Like similar constructs with which the Sharu civilization covered every planet in their home [[Star system/Legends|system]] of [[Rafa system/Legends|Rafa]] and planted on other worlds in the [[Centrality/Legends|Centrality]] region and beyond, the [[pyramid]] was built of iridescent, indestructible [[Plastic/Legends|plastic]], and featured sharp edges.<ref name="Builders" />

==History==
Around [[100,000 BBY/Legends|100,000 BBY]],<ref name="Time" /> the [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] Sharu civilization controlled the Rafa system, from which they originated, as well as the surrounding region, which would later become known as the Centrality. They covered every astronomical body in their home system with pyramids and other constructs made from a plastic that was both indestructible and iridescent. In a brief period of expansionism, the Sharu planted pyramids on other planets in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] as far Coreward as Aargau, a world that was still in its prehistory. The sharp-edged pyramid they built on that world would later become known as the Dawn Pyramid of Aargau. The Sharu later withdrew to their home system, buried their [[City/Legends|cities]], and drained their intellects, an act some believed was in response to the threat of the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestial]] civilization that controlled much of the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="Atlas" />

As Aargau's own civilization grew, the Dawn Pyramid inspired the planet's architectural theme. It had been standing on for [[10,000 BBY|ninety millennia]] when the [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Vicendi]] composed the ''[[Arturum Galactinum]]'' commemorating the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[25,000 BBY/Legends|15,000th anniversary]]. Vicendi added the Dawn Pyramid to his list of [[Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy]] in the ''Arturum Galactinum'', a list that focused on [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]]-built items, and (as was later criticised) biased towards antiquity and prolific Core Worlds&mdash;two categories within which the Dawn Pyramid of Aargau definitely fell.<ref name="Atlas" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Dawn Pyramid of Aargau has thus far been mentioned only in one [[canon]] publication, [[2009]]'s ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', which was written by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Daniel Wallace]]. In the book's "Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy" entry, the Dawn Pyramid is listed alongside items from previous ''[[Star Wars]]'' publications such as the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace]] on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and the [[Valley of Royalty]] on [[Duro/Legends|Duro]], as well as other first-time mentions.
